claude.sample_unit: patient records (VUMC n=58,817; MIMIC-IV-ED n=363,145) with simulated clinician acceptance

links.outcome: Human-AI collaborative AUROC with suppression versus human alone
links.effect: When ML outperforms humans, suppression outperforms the human alone (P < 8.2 × 10-6) and at least does not degrade fairness.
links.quote: When the ML outperforms humans, suppression outperforms the human alone (P < 8.2 × 10-6) and at least does not degrade fairness.

links.outcome: Overreliance of clinicians on ML predictions affecting performance and fairness
links.effect: Suppression of poor ML predictions via an auditor model mitigates overreliance; it improved collaborative performance when ML outperformed humans, and uncertainty quantification improved performance.
links.quote: Clinicians interacting with these systems can perpetuate such unfairness by overreliance.

unlisted_practices: Auditor model that suppresses poor-quality ML predictions before display to clinicians
Using ML uncertainty quantification as input to the auditor/suppression model
